items.title: Startup bug bites fewer IIT, IIM alumni
items.summary: New Delhi: Fewer graduates from Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) and Indian Institutes of Management (IIMs) are taking the entrepreneurial path in 2026 compared to last year, although India's appetite for startups remains strong.Only 79 IIT alumni and 20 IIM alumni launched new tech startups between January and August this year, compared to 307 IIT graduates and 71 IIM graduates who founded startups in the entire 2025, according to Tracxn data collated for ET. The platform tracks only the year of incorporation for tech startups, so it does not have comparable January-August 2025 data.Also Read: Not Just AI - How soft skills are becoming key to getting hiredFurther, according to Tracxn data, 6,353 tech startups were founded until August this year, compared with 3,969 in the whole of 2025."The increase in the number of startups being founded is a positive sign, but the real question is who is making that transition. The fact that we are not seeing a meaningful increase in founders from the IITs and IIMs suggests there is still a large, untapped pool of talent," said Vikram Gupta, founder and managing partner, IvyCap Ventures.Also Read: Centre to tap IITs, NITs for nuclear tech courses to power India's 100 GW dream135376542AI & Layoffs as Decisive Factors"If India wants to build the next generation of enduring companies, entrepreneurship must become a more viable career choice for a much wider talent pool," Gupta said.According to Saakshi Gera, managing director at Kedaara Capital, startups are increasing largely because artificial intelligence (AI) and no-code tools have dramatically reduced the cost of launching a venture, while layoffs have made entrepreneurship a more viable fallback option."But volume isn't quality. Investors continue to prioritise sustainable unit economics, and India's most credentialed talent is increasingly choosing safer, AI-adjacent jobs instead," Gera said.More IIT graduates take the entrepreneurial route than IIM alumni. India had 196,704 tech startups as of August 2026, according to Tracxn. Of these, 6,147 had at least one IIT founder, while 2,102 had at least one IIM founder."IIT alumni continue to account for a substantially larger share of startup founders than IIM alumni, which is consistent with the larger IIT alumni base and the strong engineering and deep-tech orientation of many technology startups," said Neha Singh, cofounder of Tracxn. "The technical founders have the tendency to initiate ventures early, often complemented by business expertise from IIM graduates or other professionals as companies scale."For the study, the market intelligence platform considered alumni from IITs including Bombay, Delhi, Kharagpur, Kanpur, Madras, Roorkee, Jodhpur, Hyderabad, Guwahati, BHU (Varanasi), Mandi, Bhubaneswar and ISM Dhanbad, as well as IIMs at Ahmedabad, Bangalore, Calcutta, Indore, Lucknow, Udaipur, Nagpur, Kashipur, Sirmaur and Sambalpur. According to Tracxn, it takes time to fully incorporate a company formally. "The full incorporation figures as well as the final share for startups founded in 2026 will only be known later. This may rise to some extent," said Singh.

items.title: US stocks slide: Amazon, Intel, Nvidia fall
items.summary: US stock market today: US stocks fell for the second day in a row on Friday, October 30, as investors worried about the health of the AI trade. At 10:58 AM ET, the Dow Jones was at 52,113.50, down 229.06 points or 0.44%. The S&P 500 was at 7,621.06, down 99.33 points or 1.29%. The Nasdaq was at 25,623.29, down 561.44 points or 2.14%.Why is the US stock market down today?Two earnings reports, from Amazon and Intel, came after Thursday’s closing bell and are pulling the market down this morning.Thursday was already weak. All three major indexes closed lower, and the Nasdaq lost 1.6% after Alphabet’s results disappointed. Amazon and Alphabet both posted rare earnings misses. Alphabet had its worst day in over 20 years.Amazon missed estimates on both revenue and profit. Its free cash flow also fell because of heavy spending on AI. Intel dropped sharply after giving a weak outlook for the fourth quarter.Chip stocks fell across the board. AMD lost 9%, Marvell 6% and Broadcom 5%. Micron and Nvidia each gave up more than 3%. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), which holds Intel and AMD as its two biggest positions, was down 7%.Crypto stocks also took a hit. Bitcoin fell to around $76,600 from a high near $82,000 on Thursday. Strategy (MSTR) was down 10%, Coinbase (COIN) 12% and Robinhood (HOOD) 8%.In other markets, WTI crude was above $104 a barrel, up about 2%. Gold fell to around $3,920, close to its lowest level since last November. The 10-year Treasury yield stayed at 4.94%.Intel stock price today: why the chipmaker is down nearly 30%Intel (INTC) is the worst performer on the S&P 500 today. At 10:58 AM ET it traded at $66.52, down $25.55 or 27.75%. Earlier in the session it fell about 30%, to below $65. That is a price the stock has not seen since spring.The fall comes after a big run. Intel was up roughly 250% this year through Thursday’s close, and had recently crossed levels last seen in 2000.The trigger was the company’s outlook. Intel expects fourth-quarter revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion and GAAP profit of 10 cents a share. Both are below the average estimate tracked by Visible Alpha. This overshadowed third-quarter numbers that were better than expected. CEO Lip-Bu Tan said the company faces “headwinds across the PC industry” and is finding it hard to meet “extremely high AI driven demand.”Intel’s foundry business, which makes chips for other companies, is also under watch. Its revenue rose nearly 60% year on year in Q3, but it posted an operating loss of nearly $1.9 billion.Valuation is another worry. Before the fall, Intel traded at more than 50 times estimated 2027 earnings, well above its peer group average. Morgan Stanley, which rates the stock neutral, cut its price target to $75 from $84. The Visible Alpha average target is around $90.High trending stocks today: Amazon, Nvidia, Reddit and moreAmazon (AMZN) traded at $239.31, down 1.84%. Third-quarter revenue rose nearly 12% from a year ago to about $202 billion. Net income fell, partly because last year’s quarter had gains from its stake in Anthropic. Amazon still expects AWS revenue growth run rates above 40% in both 2027 and 2028. The stock is up just 3% this year, while the S&P 500 is up 11%.Nvidia (NVDA) was at $207.25, down 3%. Alphabet (GOOGL) was at $280.64, down 1.12%, and CoreWeave (CRWV) was at $55.48, down 8.65%. SpaceX (SPCX) was at $138.52, down 3.73%, and Nokia (NOK) was at $8.66, down 6.98%.Three internet stocks also fell after their Q3 results. Reddit (RDDT) dropped 24%, Roblox (RBLX) 16% and Pinterest (PINS) 6%.Acumen Pharmaceuticals (ABOS) fell 87.47% to $0.29.A few stocks rose. TNL Mediagene (TNMG) gained 24.26% to $3.79 and Rivian (RIVN) added 5.41% to $12.07.

items.title: Binance’s $6.3B crypto heist: Who’s behind it?
items.summary: Binance hack: Hackers linked to North Korea are the main suspects in the theft of about $6.36 billion from Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange. US blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs says the group is TraderTraitor, which it calls North Korea’s elite hacking unit. Binance has not confirmed this yet.Who is behind the Binance hack?TRM Labs published its findings on Thursday. It says the attacker moved about $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across ten blockchains, most of it in around 20 minutes. If the figure holds, this is the largest crypto theft on record.Investigation update: Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach. This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it. We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them.Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe.We are still on track towards the expected timeline to resume the withdrawal service in 45 hours. Deposits remain unaffected.The outflows ceased when we paused withdrawal service earlier. We are still working with partners to freeze many of the impacted assets, and have frozen around $3 billion thus far.We will continue to provide further updates through official Binance channels as more verified information becomes available.— Binance (@binance) October 30, 2026TRM says it blames TraderTraitor “with high confidence,” based on on-chain and off-chain intelligence. It also says several features of the attack match earlier North Korea-linked thefts, including the Bybit hack.Chainalysis, another blockchain analytics firm, has a similar view. Its co-founder and CEO, Jonathan Levin, wrote on X that the hack was likely done by TraderTraitor.Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea. https://t.co/NIX65d8FpF— USA TODAY (@USATODAY) October 30, 2026Binance has not named anyone. A company spokesperson said only that it is working with law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of the criminals and bring them to justice.Is TraderTraitor a state-backed group?TRM describes TraderTraitor as a unit of North Korea, which would make it state-backed. No government has confirmed its role in the Binance case so far. The link comes from private security firms.The Bybit case offers some background. In February last year, Bybit lost $1.5 billion in a hack. The FBI said North Korea and TraderTraitor were responsible.Experts say North Korea turned to crypto theft because it needs foreign currency. Strict UN sanctions have hurt its economy, and the money is believed to help fund its nuclear programme.In December 2022, South Korea’s spy agency said North Korean hackers had stolen around $1.1 billion in crypto and other digital assets in the previous five years, more than half of it in 2022 alone.How the theft happened and what Binance says nowBinance first said the attacker may have got in through a compromised laptop belonging to an employee or contractor, which allowed unauthorised withdrawal requests. A later check found more “points of breach,” the company said. It also said it found no evidence that any wallet private key had leaked.Kok Tin Gan, CEO of cybersecurity firm NyxLab, believes a single signature may have given the attacker a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet. A hot wallet is one connected to the internet. He questioned why stronger approval controls were not in place.Binance says it froze roughly $3 billion of the affected assets with help from blockchain partners. Deposits were not affected. Withdrawals are suspended and should resume in a day or two.The company says it will cover all losses and will share more technical details once its investigation ends.Changpeng Zhao, who founded Binance, posted on X that “User funds are safe!” He said it does look like a hack, and that as a shareholder he expects all funds to be fully covered. Zhao pleaded guilty in 2023 to a felony linked to failing to prevent money laundering on the platform and stepped down as CEO. President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.

items.title: Can't brand consensual intimacy as rape after a relationship fails: SC
items.summary:
Concerned over the rising trend of filing criminal cases after the failure of relationships, the Supreme Court on Friday said that physical intimacy during good times cannot be branded as rape later just because the alliance soured or broke.
A bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahdevan, which discharged a Kerala resident man of charges of rape and cheating, said there is a need to distinguish between cases where sexual consent is legally void from the very outset as it was obtained through deliberate deception and fraud, and where a person experiences retrospective regret for past consensual acts simply because of the end of a relationship.
"In such cases, physical intimacy that occurred during the currency of a functioning relationship cannot be retrospectively branded as an act of rape merely because the relationship soured and no longer subsists," the bench said.
Such reflections in hindsight on their own are unfortunate and cannot constitute a consensual relationship as a .

Helicopter with 6 aboard crashes in Joshimath
items.summary: A helicopter, operated by Trans Bharat Aviation and travelling from Badrinath to Dehradun has gone missing with six people on board, with Uttarakhand Chief Minister confirming it has crashed near Joshimath in Chamoli district on Friday."We have received the unfortunate news of a helicopter crash near Chayee village, close to Joshimath. A joint rescue operation is being conducted by the district administration, disaster management department, and SDRF," CM Pushkar Singh Dhami said in a post on social media platform X.Uttarakhand Civil Aviation Development Authority (UCADA) also confirmed the news.— pushkardhami (@pushkardhami) The helicopter, bearing call sign VT-HCX, took off at around 1:14 pm. Its tracking signal was also lost, and its current location could not be ascertained. Teams from the Indian Army, Chamoli district administration and the State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) have been mobilised for search and rescue operations, UCADA said.There were six people on board, including the pilot, Capt. Himanshu, and five passengers identified as Prathapa, Arun, Shankar Gowda, Sudheer K and H.S. Natraja. As a precautionary measure, the entire fleet of Trans Bharat Aviation has been grounded, UCADA said.The wreckage of the aircraft is yet to be located, with persistent rainfall and poor visibility hampering search operations. Two other choppers have been pressed into service to locate the missing helicopter. According to PTI, the helicopter is reportedly operated by Charlie X-ray Company. A team from the district administration is currently searching for the missing helicopter, according to ANI news agency.The Chamoli district administration confirmed that there were six people on the helicopter, including five passengers and one pilot.— ANI (@ANI) According to preliminary information as per media reports, the helicopter is suspected to have crashed near Chayi village, behind Hathi Pahar in the Joshimath area. It was travelling from Badrinath to Phata, as per reports.Two other helicopters have been deployed to trace the missing aircraft and locate its wreckage. Police, SDRF, Army and ITBP personnel have been dispatched to the site for relief and rescue operations, officials said.Information about a possible helicopter crash landing was received from the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) of Joshimath at 2:21 pm, officials said.The Trans Bharat helicopter was flying from Badrinath to Sahastradhara and had five passengers and a pilot on board. Its location was showing near the Army Camp above Chai village in the Joshimath area, Sub-Inspector Manohar Kanyal of Joshimath police post said. Details of the incident, including whether the helicopter had crashed or made an emergency landing, were not immediately available.

Musk warns ‘game over’ if Dems sweep 2028
items.summary: SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has warned that a Democratic sweep of the US House of Representatives, Senate and presidency in 2028 could bring major changes to the country’s political system.In a post on X on Thursday, Musk said such an outcome would be “game over for America” and urged voters to support Republican Senate candidates in the November 3 midterm elections.“My biggest concern is that if there is a clean sweep by Democrats of the House, Senate and Presidency in 2028, they will: Make DC and Puerto Rico states to gain a strong majority in the Senate; Open the borders and legalize everyone living in America illegally to cement a permanent majority; Increase the size of the Supreme Court to gain an immediate majority,” Musk said.— elonmusk (@elonmusk) “This would result in America becoming a permanent one-party state and the end of democracy in any meaningful sense of the word,” he said.“All that is needed to ensure this doesn’t happen is 51 Republican senators in 2029. That is why you should vote for Republican senators this election. Other reasons are irrelevant compared to this one,” Musk added.His remarks came as he emerged as the largest individual political donor in US history, having spent more than $442 million on Republican campaigns and political groups ahead of the midterm elections.The Hill reported that Musk contributed an additional $76.8 million to his America PAC over the past month. The contribution took his total spending on the upcoming elections beyond $442 million. America PAC received the funds over about a week in October.Musk had already spent $366 million supporting Republican candidates and groups. He established America PAC during the 2024 election cycle.According to campaign finance filings cited by CBS News, Musk donated $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund through two contributions in September. The super PAC supports Republican Senate candidates and later transferred the money to a Texas-based political action committee backing Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton.Musk donated $75 million on September 9 and another $83 million about two weeks later. The contributions accounted for more than half of the Senate Leadership Fund’s receipts in the third quarter, CBS News reported.He also donated $10 million to the pro-Paxton Lone Star Liberty PAC through his trust. In addition, Musk gave $20 million to the Congressional Leadership Fund, $10 million to the Republican Governors Association and $2 million to the Republican Attorneys General Association.The Texas Senate race is among the closely contested contests where Musk has directed his political spending. Republican candidate and state Attorney General Ken Paxton is facing Democratic challenger James Talarico.Musk’s America PAC has also supported Republican candidates in competitive congressional races.His latest spending marks a return to large-scale political donations after he spent more than $250 million supporting President Donald Trump and other Republican candidates during the 2024 election cycle. His involvement had appeared uncertain after his public feud with Trump last year.The November 3 midterm elections will decide control of both chambers of Congress and could determine the future of Trump’s legislative agenda.A CBS News poll published on October 25 projected that Democrats could win 229 seats in the House as inflation and economic concerns influence voters. The estimate could extend into the 230s, although Republicans retain a narrow path to holding the majority.The Democratic lead has remained steady in recent weeks, but CBS News said there was no growing electoral wave.Trump said on October 27 that he would respect the results of the midterm elections if they were conducted honestly, while warning that he could use his veto power if necessary.“We'll figure a way. I have a strong veto. I hope that won't be the case, but if it is, that's happened before… I will — if they're honest elections,” Trump told reporters.The election comes as the administration faces economic concerns and declining approval ratings. The Wall Street Journal reported in September that Trump’s approval rating had fallen to 37%, the lowest recorded for a president approaching midterm elections in the publication’s polling history dating back to 1990.

The government has notified the National Social Security Board for unorganised workers and gig and platform workers, which will design, monitor, and recommend targeted welfare schemes to bridge the social security gap.
Gig workers are those who perform work or participate in a work arrangement and earn from such activities outside the traditional employer-employee relationship.
Platform workers are those who engage in work through or with online platforms.

items.title: Trump's grip on Congress may be slipping
items.summary: Donald Trump's grip on Congress is starting to look a little shaky. Four days before the US midterm elections, major polls show Democrats with a clear national advantage in the fight for the House of Representatives. The Senate remains more competitive, but new CNN polling has put Democrats ahead in several key races that could decide control of the chamber.Also Read| What's at stake for Trump, his opponents and 2028 White House raceRepublicans currently control both chambers of Congress. Democrats need a net gain of three seats in the House and four in the Senate to take control.US Midterm Elections 2026: What do the latest polls reveal?The latest surveys from major news organisations and pollsters show Democrats leading the national congressional ballot by 8 to 10 percentage points.PollField datesDemocratic leadReuters/IpsosOct 22–2653% to 44% — D+9CBS News/YouGovOct 21–2353% to 45% — D+8NPR/PBS News/MaristOct 19–2052% to 44% — D+8CNN/SSRSOct 15–1849% to 39% — D+10ABC News/Washington Post/IpsosOct 9–1352% to 44% — D+8AP-NORCOct 8–1247% to 38% — D+9The latest national poll in this group is the Reuters/Ipsos survey, which interviewed voters through October 26. The AP-NORC, ABC News/Washington Post and CNN national polls were conducted earlier and should not be read as a measure of voter sentiment on October 30.The AP-NORC poll found that 47% of voters wanted Democrats to control the House, compared with 38% who wanted Republicans to remain in charge. The ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos survey found an even wider preference for Democratic control: 59% wanted the next Congress to act as a check on Trump, while 35% preferred Republicans to support his agenda.Trump's Approval Rating: How are American voters viewing the President?Trump's approval rating is weak across the major surveys. AP-NORC found that 36% voters approved of his job performance, while 64% disapproved. The ABC News/Washington Post/Ipsos poll recorded 33% approval and 66% disapproval.The Reuters/Ipsos poll, conducted most recently, put Trump’s approval at 32%. Only 25% approved of his handling of the economy and 20% approved of his handling of the cost of living.Economic concerns are central to the election. In the AP-NORC poll, 85% of voters called the economy an important issue when deciding how to vote, while 84% said the same about the cost of living.The NPR/PBS News/Marist poll found that 44% of likely voters viewed their congressional vote mainly as a vote against Trump. Only 21% said their vote was mainly in favour of him.CNN polling shows Democratic path to Senate majorityThe Senate remains harder for Democrats because they must win several Republican-leaning states. CNN’s latest battleground polls, released on October 29, showed Democrats ahead in four important Senate races:Texas: James Talarico led Ken Paxton, 49% to 43%.Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed led Mike Rogers, 49% to 42%.Kansas: Adam Hamilton led Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, 49% to 45%.Maine: Troy Jackson led Republican incumbent Susan Collins, 49% to 45%.The Kansas and Maine leads were within the margin of error. The Texas and Michigan results gave Democrats a stronger advantage, although neither race was certain. The CNN results give Democrats a possible route to the four Senate gains they need. But they would still have to perform strongly in other closely contested races, including Alaska, Iowa, Ohio and South Carolina.Republicans have an advantage in the Senate map because several competitive seats are in states Trump carried in 2024. Democrats therefore need to win multiple races where the presidential vote favoured the Republican Party.Also Read| Are educated Republican districts going extinct?House is more favourable to DemocratsCBS News’ latest House model, based on its October 21–23 poll and district-level data, put Democrats on course to win 229 seats. It said Republicans still had a narrow path to retain control.The model also warned that the Democratic lead had not expanded in recent weeks and that voters who were uncertain about voting tended to lean more Republican.That makes turnout critical. Reuters/Ipsos found that 46% of Democrats were very enthusiastic about voting, compared with 30% of Republicans. The NPR/PBS News/Marist poll also found higher overall enthusiasm among Democratic likely voters.Reading the tea leavesThe latest major national polls point to Democratic gains and put the House within the party’s reach. The Senate remains unsettled, but CNN’s newest battleground surveys show Democrats with a possible path to a majority.The numbers do not guarantee a Democratic sweep. The result will depend on turnout, late-deciding voters and whether Democratic candidates can convert narrow leads in Republican-leaning states into victories.

items.title: Rahul Gandhi backs IDBI Bank staff, questions sale to Canada's Fairfax
items.summary:
Amid the IDBI bank disinvestment row, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has expressed solidarity with the bank employees and questioned the government's decision to sell off the profitable public bank to a Canadian firm.
The Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha asserted that public banks are not assets to be sold off, they are tools to build the nation.
In a letter addressed to members of the IDBI Bank family, Gandhi said that in March last year, a group of IDBI bank employees came to meet him in Parliament House and asked him a simple question as to why the government is selling a bank that they had made profitable.
"I took that question to the Lok Sabha. I asked why a profitable public bank was being sold and how its employees and depositors would be protected. The government gave no reason. Now it has decided to sell IDBI Bank to Fairfax, a Canadian company," Gandhi said.

items.title: India remains growth engine; Super El Nino impact yet to materialise: IMF
items.summary:
The IMF on Thursday said the impact of weather events such as the Super El Nino was yet to materialise for India, which remains the engine of growth for the world economy.
The IMF listed lower crop yields, increased food price inflation and its impact on the purchasing power of households in India due to the Super El Nino.
"So these are risks that we see that India faces, but right now those risks have not materialised," IMF Communications Director Julie Kozack told a press conference here.
She said the IMF will reassess India's growth projections in the January World Economic Outlook update after the risks posed by the weather event materialise.
Earlier this month, the IMF raised India's growth forecast for fiscal year 2027 and fiscal year 2028 to 7 per cent, from the 6.4 per cent and 6.7 per cent projections respectively made in July.
"So, we see it really as a risk going forward, and of course depending on whether that risk materialises, we will reassess our growth projections

Russian crude, which became a significant component of India's oil import basket after the Russia-Ukraine war, has lost some of its earlier pricing appeal as elevated freight costs eroded its advantage on a delivered basis.

TVS Motor Company plans to increase its electric two-wheeler manufacturing capacity to 80,000 units per month by the end of March 2027 to meet strong demand for electric scooters, according to a senior company official.
"Now we are also enhancing the capacity. We are now operating at around 60-65,000 units. We have already planned for the next level of capacity expansion to about 80,000 units," TVS Motor Chief Executive Officer KN Radhakrishnan told investors.
Electric vehicle penetration has been growing at a very strong pace in the two-wheeler space. Penetration in the overall two-wheeler market has been around 11-12 per cent, while it has crossed the 20 per cent mark in the scooter segment.
TVS Motor is currently the market leader in the electric two-wheeler segment.
Its major competitor, Bajaj Auto, is also enhancing Chetak capacity to 80,000 units. Ather Energy is also increasing capacity at its existing facility to over 41,000 units while its new facility is coming up.

items.title: The price of what low-skilled workers know
items.summary: It is heartening to see Indian workers helping generate the data that will drive the next generation of robots and artificial intelligence. Every month, a fresh batch of images does the rounds on LinkedIn and X: Indian factory employees with cameras strapped to their heads, their every movement recorded to train AI systems. The message? Tasks once thought resistant to automation are suddenly within AI’s reach. But these images of Indian workers wearing cameras should provoke something more serious than technological excitement or dystopian alarm. They should provoke a strategic question: Who owns data? Who builds models? Who controls these machines, and where does the resulting value accumulate?The instinctive reaction, of course, is enthusiasm, and these images are easy to celebrate. Yes, AI training is happening in India, and Indian workers are part of it. Gig, factory, and service workers are capturing ordinary physical tasks from a first-person perspective, and thousands of hours of Indian movement are becoming training material for the next generation of AI. Participation is not however synonymous with power. The important question to ask is not whether artificial intelligence is being trained in India. It’s what India is contributing to the process, on what terms, and who will ultimately own the productive assets created from it.Also read | Your boss may soon know what you’re asking Claude to do at workSeveral reports show that filming factory workers is fast becoming normal across Indian cities. In Gurugram and Nagpur, for example, workers are being recorded as they sew, adjust loom tension, and clear machine jams, or are simply under surveillance as they work. Similar data collection is spreading across the service economy. Human Archive, a Silicon Valley-based physical AI data startup, says it has deployed more than 1,000 headsets through partners in India and pays a base rate of $1 an hour for egocentric data collection, acknowledging that its Indian network helps keep compensation lower. Put simply, India’s cheap labour is becoming cheap machine-training data, too.The ambitions extend far beyond individual experiments and individual startups. EgoLab, an Indian startup which has been collecting first-person footage from Indian factories, was acquired in 2026 by US-registered Build Artificial Intelligence Inc. EgoLab's own material, reviewed by scroll had described their ambition to collect $100 million in footage from 100 million factory workers across major Indian states and sectors, including textiles, automobiles, chemicals, electronics, FMCG, and steel. BuildAI's published current roadmap similarly includes an ego-centric 100-million-dataset target for October 2027.These are not outcomes, but these ambitions reveal the intended scale of how India's data is being converted into a dataset that can be aggregated, transferred, and used globally. A worker wearing a camera records two outputs. The immediate output is the product of labour and information about how that labour is performed. In the future AI economy, the work is just not generating output; it is also recording the work, which can generate capital in the future.Also read | Zoho’s Sridhar Vembu sees a painful rebalancing of jobs in the AI ageThis is very relevant for a country where 88% of the workers are employed in occupations classified as low competency. This classification may make sense within the conventional labour market, but the same task has become extraordinarily valuable from the perspective of physical AI. Large language models could learn from vast stores of digitized text, images, and code; Physical AI there is no equivalent archive for much of what humans know about operating in the real world. Robotic Machines still struggle with actions people perform almost automatically: adjusting grips and pressure, manipulating unfamiliar objects, coordinating hands and tools, recovering from mistakes, and adapting when physical, emotional, and other conditions change. Therefore, what is routine knowledge for a human worker can become frontier knowledge for a machine. India's workforce is not only a source of inexpensive labour; it is also a potentially enormous reservoir for the demonstration that physical AI still needs to learn how the world works. However, a country that built its IT boom on labour-cost arbitrage, in practice, introduces a striking inversion: cheaper labour once reduced the incentive to automate. Now, if human demonstration can also be acquired cheaply, low wages may also help reduce the cost of teaching automation itself.In other words, India’s cheap labour no longer simply competes with automation. It could also cut the global cost of training robots and large language models. The point to contemplate is not merely whether machines will displace workers. It’s whether the knowledge workers bring becomes a strategic resource whose value is realised elsewhere. History isn’t reassuring here and we know that economies that supplied essential raw materials often had little control over the industries built around them, and their competitiveness suffered. That’s why Frank Herbert’s Dune offers such a valuable metaphor.In Dune, Arrakis, a barren desert planet, possesses spice, the indispensable resource on which an advanced civilisation relies for interstellar travel. However, owning this resource does not automatically mean dominance over the system built around it. Instead, others coordinate its extraction, trade, and conversion into power. India faces a version of that dilemma in the emerging physical AI economy. Its spice is the vast stock of embodied knowledge held by its workers - the accumulated judgement, dexterity, and experience in how tasks are performed. Indian companies can collect and annotate worker data but risk missing out on valuable layers if India remains just a raw knowledge supplier, as key datasets, models, robotics, software, platforms, and machines are mainly owned elsewhere. India is repeating an old development pattern in a new technological form.India’s previous outsourcing boom was built on supplying labour to the West. Physical AI raises the prospect that India will now also supply the knowledge embedded in that labour, captured as data and used to train robots, machines, and large language models worldwide. The strategic challenge for India, then, is to make sure it doesn’t remain merely the source of that input. That means guarding its data privacy and sovereignty, while also developing its own models, robotic capabilities, and intellectual property built on that data.India doesn’t need to stop the flow of spice. It just needs to make sure it doesn’t become merely Arrakis.(Amit Kapoor is chair & Sheen Zutshi isresearch manager atInstitute for Competitiveness.).

items.title: Tilak Varma opens up on batting role as India chase 5-0 series win over NZ
items.summary:
India vice-captain Tilak Varma says moving down from number three to five in the batting order has led to a slight change in his mindset and he now eyes boundaries from ball one instead of trying to settle in first.
Tilak has built a reputation of being a chase master over the last 12 months. Even in the second T20I against New Zealand, he pulled off a tense chase batting alongside Nitish Reddy. India have taken an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match series.
"I already had the power game; I have scored runs at number three as well. Now, batting at number five or six, I think about going for a boundary off the very first ball only if it's there to be hit," he said ahead of the fourth T20I here.
"Otherwise, I focus on taking the game deep. I take a bit more time. Initially, I focus on singles and doubles, finding gaps for fours or two runs," he added.
While pacing the run chase, Tilak says he likes to play with the psyche of the bowlers, who are under more pressure than batters.

The Supreme Court on Thursday refused to issue any direction to the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) mandating public disclosure of ultimate beneficial owners and portfolios of alternative investment funds (AIFs), foreign portfolio investors and their intermediaries in India.
A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna, R Mahadevan and DK Upadhyaya, hearing a plea filed by TMC MP Mahua Moitra, said there was no legal regime or any framework in place for any full public disclosure about ultimate beneficial owners.
The bench initially questioned Moitra for filing such a petition, saying she could have raised the issue in Parliament and sought a discussion on it.
The top court said it cannot issue any mandamus without any regime in place and disposed of the plea.
"Had there been any legal regime and the SEBI was not following it, the court can direct for compliance but in the absence of any framework or legal regime, the court cannot issue any mandamus," it observed.

items.summary:
When Donald Trump was running for president two years ago, Americans' television screens were filled with images of migrant chaos. There were tent camps on both sides of the border, caravans of people trudging through Central America and concerns about newcomers overwhelming social services.
That turmoil faded as President Joe Biden tightened immigration enforcement after Trump clamped down even more. items.title: Neet paper leak case: Delhi court reserves order on framing charges
items.summary:
A Delhi court on Thursday reserved its order on framing of charges against 14 accused in the NEET-UG paper leak case.
Special Judge Ajay Gupta said the order would be pronounced on November 18.
Earlier this year, the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) had filed a chargesheet against 13 accused in the present fast-track court dealing with "criminal cases arising from paper leaks as well as the use of other unfair means in public examinations".
The agency also filed a supplementary chargesheet against the 14th accused, Sheshrav Bajrang Suryawanshi alias Raj Suryawanshi, a resident of Nanded in Maharashtra, who was arrested on September 2.
The National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate), or NEET-UG, is conducted by the NTA for medical aspirants.
On May 12, the NTA cancelled the NEET-UG held on May 3 amid allegations of paper leak. A re-examination was conducted on June 21.

items.title: Domestic aviation industry may post losses of ₹38,000 cr in FY27: Icra
items.summary:
The Indian aviation industry is expected to post net losses of Rs 36,000-38,000 crore in the current fiscal, compared to estimated net losses of Rs 28,000-30,000 crore in the previous year, ratings agency ICRA said on Thursday.
The losses were primarily driven by moderation in passenger traffic growth, rising aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices and forex losses arising from the sharp depreciation of the Indian rupee, it said.
The onset of the war in West Asia in late February 2026 is expected to dampen air passenger traffic growth in FY27, ICRA said.
Additionally, increased costs due to depreciation of the Indian Rupee against the US dollar, elevated ATF prices and a rise in lease rentals amid continued aircraft deliveries are projected to cause a net loss of Rs 36,000-38,000 crore in this fiscal.
These cost escalations may not be adequately passed on to passengers through fare hikes, it said.

items.title: Ready to share 'battle-tested' anti-terror expertise with Asean: Rajnath
items.summary:
India is ready to share its "battle-tested" counter-terror expertise with ASEAN and its dialogue partners, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said on Thursday as he described Operation Sindoor as a declaration of New Delhi's clear approach against state-sponsored terrorist activities.
The defence minister also said that India supports an Indo-Pacific that is secure and resilient -- one where peace and stability are not merely aspirations, but the outcome of collective efforts.

items.title: EPFO plans to invest in startups, AIFs
items.summary: The Employees Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) is working on guidelines to enable investments in alternative investment funds (AIFs), five years after the government cleared the retirement body’s entry into these high-growth asset classes and startups, The Times of India reported on Thursday.The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) discussed a proposal to allocate up to 3% of EPFO’s fresh annual accretions to Category I and Category II AIFs at an investment committee meeting last Thursday, the report said.The move could mark a shift in how the retirement fund body deploys workers’ savings, allowing it to gain exposure to startups and other growth-oriented investments beyond its traditional debt instruments.The proposal will now be placed before the central board of trustees, headed by Labour Minister Mansukh Mandaviya, in November, according to the report.The development follows a September letter from the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT) seeking EPFO’s participation in the recently launched Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0.The proposal prompted discussions on a broader framework for investments in AIFs, the report added.Initially, EPFO is considering routing investments through institutional entities such as the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund (NIIF) and the Small Industries Development Bank of India’s (SIDBI) Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0.Under the investment pattern notified by the finance ministry, EPFO can invest up to 5% of its fresh accretions in asset-backed and trust-structured investments. It has not yet invested in SEBI-regulated Category I and Category II AIFs.Category I AIFs typically support startups, small businesses, infrastructure and venture capital, while Category II funds include private equity, real estate and private debt funds.The proposed framework includes safeguards such as a minimum AIF corpus of Rs 100 crore, limits on exposure to individual funds, restrictions on investments in foreign-incorporated entities and requirements for fund manager independence.EPFO manages around Rs 30 lakh crore in retirement savings for nearly 30 crore members, the report said.

items.title: Putin seeks new tax revenue to fund Russia's war as budget deficit swells
items.summary:
With Russia's invasion of Ukraine intensifying the strain on state finances, President Vladimir Putin is reaching for cash to fund his government and the war, squeezing tax revenue from an economy that's increasingly skewed toward the military - while civilian needs take a back seat.
The country's 2027-2029 state budget, which will be taken up Thursday in the rubber-stamp parliament, is accompanied by a string of tax hikes announced after the September parliamentary elections.
While last year the Kremlin went for a broad tax increase, raising value-added taxes at the cash register and making more small businesses pay VAT, this cash grab hits a narrower segment: mining companies and better-off citizens with investment income, property sales and bank accounts.
The budget deficit this year has swelled beyond forecasts due to lavish military spending and tepid economic growth amid sanctions, high interest rates for non-military companies, labour shortages and Ukrainian strikes on oil ..

He breaks down home country bias, why up to 70% of an Indian household’s spending is effectively linked to the dollar, and how regulatory changes in GIFT City, the tax harmonisation on long-term capital gains and the coming SEBI rules are making global investing easier for the mass affluent. He also argues that global investing is far more than the Magnificent 7, covering small and midcaps in the US and Europe, gold miners, nuclear power, data centres, commercial property and bonds. On India, he opens up about Marcellus’s four-year underperformance phase and what it taught him: broaden the portfolio beyond two themes, trim positions when prices run far ahead of earnings, and stay open to new sectors. He explains why he is radically overweight India despite the global allocation, why large cap quality looks the cheapest in 10 to 15 years, and why the small and midcap obsession could cost investors dearly. He also talks about the structural shift in the economy from IT services to manufacturing exports, rising household debt, the risk of another NBFC credit cycle, and why he calls banks a tricky but potentially rewarding trade. He wraps up with practical advice on handling market noise, avoiding FOMO and keeping your sanity..

items.title: Rajnath Singh strengthens JAI partnership
items.summary: Highlighting how India has maintained close ties with its partners in the Pacific Ocean, Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh on Thursday posted a picture with his counterparts, Japanese Minister of Defense Shinjirō Koizumi, and the Australian Minister for Defence Richard Marles. "JAI: Japan, Australia, India", the Defence Minister posted on X, with him holding hands of both Marles and Koizumi, as he stood in the middle.  Earlier on Wednesday, Singh held a meeting with Koizumi on the sidelines of the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu, the Philippines, and discussed ways to strengthen bilateral defence cooperation.In a post on X, Singh said, "Happy to meet with the Minister of Defense of Japan, Mr. Koizumi Shinjiro, on the sidelines of the 13th ADMM-Plus in Cebu, Philippines."Highlighting the importance of cooperation between the two countries, the Defence Minister said, "Our shared commitment remains vital for a free, open, and peaceful Indo-Pacific region."Koizumi also thanked Rajnath Singh for the warm welcome and the meeting. He assured of Japan's commitment to strengthening cooperation between the two countries across various areas, including defence.On the same day, Singh held a bilateral meeting with Australian Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Richard Marles.In a post on X, Singh said the meeting provided an opportunity to review bilateral defence cooperation and discuss ways to strengthen coordination between the two countries.Emphasising the importance of bilateral ties, Singh said, "India places great value on its Comprehensive Strategic Partnership with Australia for a free, open, and secure Indo-Pacific."Both leaders also exchanged gifts as a gesture of goodwill and friendship. During the meeting, Singh also invited Marles to attend Aero India-2027, scheduled to be held in Bengaluru in February 2027.The ADMM is the highest defence consultative and cooperative mechanism in ASEAN. ADMM-Plus is a platform for ASEAN member states (Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste and Vietnam) and its eight Dialogue Partners (India, US, China, Russia, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand) to strengthen security and defence cooperation.

items.title: Hegseth fires top military planner even as Trump plans fresh Iran strikes
items.summary:
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has fired the Pentagon's top military planner, a defence official said Wednesday, the latest in a series of generals to be ousted and one that comes even as President Donald Trump is weighing renewed strikes on Iran in the eight-month-long war.
Army Lt Gen Brett Sylvia was removed as head of strategy, plans and policy on the Joint Chiefs of Staff. He is the second general to be ousted from the post, known in military circles as the "J5", under Hegseth. His predecessor, Lt Gen Joseph McGee, was forced to retire last October.
The defence official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive personnel matters, said there is no immediate replacement for Sylvia and no reason has been given for the firing. The move was reported earlier by The Atlantic.

Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his family arrived in Miami on Wednesday after he refused to concede the election to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and fled the country.
In a circuitous journey, Bolsonaro left for Argentina on Tuesday with his wife and two daughters, then travelled to Ecuador, according to Argentina officials and flight data. The 45-year-old senator, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, visited the White House in May, and the Trump administration approved US visas for him and his family this week.
Bolsonaro's father, Jair Bolsonaro, also fled to Florida after losing the 2022 presidential election to Lula before returning to Brazil three months later.
Flavio Bolsonaro is under investigation by Brazil's Supreme Court, accused of corruption, money laundering and tax evasion. The court had ordered him to hand over his regular and diplomatic passports by noon Tuesday. It remained unclear whether he had complied, but allies said .

global tech boom.Samsung is the world's largest maker of memory chips -- components in short supply as advanced types are snapped up for use in data centres powering artificial intelligence.Also read: South Korea fines Google, Apple a combined $47.6 million over app store payment practicesThe company posted July-September operating profit at 107.4 trillion won ($80.5 billion) -- up more than 780 percent on-year.It marked the first time any technology company had reported quarterly operating profit over 100 trillion won, Samsung said.Net profit jumped more than 510 percent from last year to 75.1 trillion won, while sales reached 195.3 trillion won.The global race to build data centres to train and run chatbots, image generators and other AI tools has turbocharged the fortunes of Samsung and other chipmakers, despite concerns that the sector may be overvalued.Samsung shares fell more than five percent on Thursday morning.Investors were disappointed by a miss of market expectations for operating profit by the semiconductor division, according to Bloomberg News.The company's memory business achieved "another record-breaking quarter by managing its product mix, with a focus on AI products, amid capacity constraints," Samsung said in a statement."Strong demand momentum for servers led to higher market prices across all applications."'Unprecedented growth'Demand-driven shortages of advanced memory chips known as HBM, used in AI systems alongside other data-crunching semiconductors, has caused their price to spike.Dilin Wu, research strategist at Pepperstone, said strong earnings from Samsung and South Korean industry rival SK hynix were "a reminder that the AI memory boom is still very real, despite all the concerns we've seen around the broader AI trade"."Chipmakers are benefiting directly from the AI investment boom, while the companies buying their chips are still trying to prove they can earn a decent return on all that spending," she told AFP earlier this week.With sky-high expectations for stellar results, record profits may not be enough to reassure market players."Ultimately, investors want to know whether there's still another leg to this memory upcycle, or whether we're getting close to peak earnings," Wu said.Samsung predicted Thursday that it would continue to feel the benefits of the AI boom.Chief financial officer Park Soon-cheol told an earnings call the company expects "unprecedented growth in memory demand in 2027, driven by accelerating competition to build AI infrastructure and the expansion of personal AI agents"."On the supply side, however, we expect difficulties in expanding... output in a short period of time through new capacity additions," he said.Chip companies focusing their efforts on profitable HBM has also fuelled shortages of the less glamorous computer memory components used in everyday consumer electronics -- driving up the price of smartphones and laptops.Shareholder returnsSamsung on Thursday detailed plans to return up to 110 trillion won to shareholders this year, including 30 trillion won in cash dividends, following an August announcement.Record profits driven by booming demand for AI memory chips have fuelled calls for greater shareholder returns, particularly after shares in tech giants such as Samsung tumbled from their June record highs amid concerns over US tech firms' AI spending.The announcement comes a day after SK hynix also announced plans to return 60 trillion won to shareholders, following the completion of a 40 trillion-won shareholder return programme.Such shareholder returns "would allow the benefits of earnings growth to translate into greater shareholder returns," said Kim Dong-won, head of KB Securities' research center."With record profits and undervaluation coexisting, the largest-ever expansion of shareholder returns would be a decisive opportunity to address the company's undervaluation and serve as a key driver of a reassessment of its market value," said Kim.

items.title: SP Group to raise $200 million to repay debt
items.summary: Shapoorji Pallonji Group is looking to raise $150 million to $200 million, according to people familiar with the matter, as the Indian conglomerate faces mounting debt obligations.SP Group plans to raise the funds through private credit by issuing more rupee bonds initially sold by its Eqyizen Investment Pvt. unit in July, said the people, who asked not be named discussing private information. About half of the proceeds will be used to repay creditors of Porteast Investment Ltd., another SP Group unit, they said. The remainder will go toward other group debt, the people said, adding that talks are at an early stage and the size and terms could change.Also read: Shapoorji Pallonji Group wants Tata Sons to consider Rs 25,000 crore share buybackThe fresh financing would help SP Group cut debt at Porteast and reduce pressure on its loan-to-value ratio, the people said. Representatives for SP Group didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.SP Group has faced increasing strain as more debt comes due and it endures a prolonged wait to monetize its assets, including a large stake in Tata Sons Pvt, where executives are locked in a battle over whether or not to list publicly. The Mistry family, which controls SP Group, is the second-largest shareholder of Tata Sons with a roughly 18.4% share.SP Group’s latest fundraising plan comes after the company borrowed about 44.5 billion rupees ($467 million) in September through Eqyizen and dollar bonds sold by another unit called Mercury Finance Co., the people familiar said. That money was used for amortization payments due at Porteast, they said. The group is seeking to complete its new financing by mid-November, the people said.

Gold FoF Curbs: What investors can do now?
items.summary: Several mutual fund houses have temporarily stopped accepting fresh investments into gold fund-of-funds (FoFs), leaving investors wondering whether they can continue investing through existing SIPs and what alternatives are available. Here is what the restrictions mean and what investors can do if they still want exposure to gold.WHAT ARE GOLD FUND-OF-FUNDS (FOFs), AND HOW DO THEY WORK?Gold FoFs are mutual fund schemes that invest in Gold ETFs rather than buying physical gold directly.When an investor puts money into a Gold FoF, the fund manager uses that money to purchase units of a Gold ETF. The Gold ETF, in turn, invests in physical gold. As a result, a Gold FoF’s value generally moves in line with gold prices.They offer a simple way to invest in gold through the mutual fund route without needing a demat account. Investors can buy and redeem units like any other mutual fund scheme while gaining exposure to changes in gold prices.WHY HAVE SOME MUTUAL FUND HOUSES RESTRICTED FRESH INVESTMENTS IN GOLD FOFs?Several fund houses have temporarily stopped accepting fresh investments in Gold FoFs from mid-October. The restrictions include fresh lump-sum investments, new SIP registrations and switch-ins, though they differ across schemes.While fund houses have not disclosed specific reasons behind the move, industry participants believe it may be linked to concerns over rising gold imports and strong inflows into gold investment products. As these ETF units are backed by physical gold, sustained inflows into such products can translate into higher demand for imported gold.Read more: Best gilt mutual funds to invest in October 2026CAN’T INVEST IN A GOLD FOF? WHAT ARE THE OTHER OPTIONS?Gold ETFs are one of the closest alternatives for investors seeking exposure to gold through market-linked investments. While there are restrictions on fresh investments in several Gold FoFs, there are none on their ETFs.Read more: Top 8 equity MFs offer double-digit gains on SIP investments since last Diwali. Do you own any?HOW ARE GOLD ETFs DIFFERENT FROM GOLD FOFs?Gold FoFs are generally more convenient for retail investors because they can be bought and redeemed like any other mutual fund scheme without requiring a demat account. Gold ETFs can only be bought and sold through a demat and trading account.Gold ETFs typically have lower costs because investors bear only the ETF’s expense ratio. In a Gold FoF, investors indirectly bear the expenses of both the FoF and the underlying ETF.Liquidity also differs. Gold ETFs can be bought and sold on stock exchanges during market hours, while Gold FoFs are purchased and redeemed at the day’s closing net asset value (NAV), like regular mutual funds.However, unlike Gold FoFs, their ETFs do not offer the convenience of a mutual fund SIP. Though many brokers have SIP facilities for buying ETFs and stocks, they are perceived to be relatively less user-friendly. Also, not all ETFs are liquid. Some of them might be trading at a premium to the ETF’s NAV.

items.title: Cyclone Arnab leaves 3 dead, damages 31 houses in Andhra Pradesh: NDRF
items.summary:
Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra coast early on Wednesday, leaving a trail of destruction with uprooted trees and electric poles and damaged roads, while two persons were electrocuted in separate instances, officials said.
The very severe cyclonic storm Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between 2 am- 8 am, before weakening into a severe cyclonic storm, the weather office said.
"The cyclone crossed the Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts to the Southwest of Yanam near latitude 16.450 N and 81.90 E, about 20 km east-northeast of Narsapur, 40 km southwest of Yanam and 60 km southwest of Kakinada," the India Meteorological Department (IMD) said in an official release.
Many parts of coastal districts received heavy rainfall, some of them in excess of 200 mm.
In its wake, Cyclone Arnab left a trail of destruction, uprooting several trees and power poles, leading to power outages in several areas. Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to restore normalcy at the .

Trump's cure for midterm woes is more Trump
items.summary: Washington: President Donald Trump likes to play make-believe with his supporters."Just close your eyes," he tells them, "and pretend I'm on the ballot."It's a typically self-involved appeal from someone who has been the center of the nation's political gravity for more than a decade. Now, he's finishing the midterms with a cross-country blitz of campaign rallies that allow him to bask in applause when he's otherwise profoundly unpopular.Also Read: Hackers target US election watchdog's filing system days before midterm pollsIn a year marked by the war with Iran, fears about artificial intelligence, redistricting fights, high energy prices and increasing concerns about the cost of living, Trump's deeply personal approach might be the election cycle's biggest gamble.Republicans still love the president, who remains dominant even as he approaches the back half of his second term. But his approval ratings are low enough to potentially sink his party and its bid to maintain control of Congress."I don't think there's anybody that wants Donald Trump out there at these rallies more than Democratic candidates," said Jessica Mackler, president of EMILY's List, which focuses on electing Democratic women who support abortion rights.Every time there's another Trump event, she said, "we look at that as a win."White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said Trump is "the unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party.""The choice has never been more clear," he said in a statement. "Doubling down on President Trump's winning, commonsense agenda, or the Democrats' extreme liberal policies and obstruction."Trump thinks the way to win elections is more TrumpIt goes far beyond a whirlwind rally schedule.The president organized even small details of the first-ever Republican midterm convention last month in Dallas, speaking both nights. He also was depicted there as the Marlboro Man, a cowboy on horseback and with a white Stetson who could ride to the rescue, on everything from baseball caps to beer cozies.Trump even has a personal spin on his blockbuster attempt to win over voters by pledging big checks if Republicans hold Congress, saying "I'll give you $5,000" even though the improbable idea would likely need lawmaker approval.Political groups associated with the president have spent at least around $277 million since Sept. 1 to help Republicans - a staggering sum that nonetheless didn't completely drain the $416 million that Trump's flagship Super PAC, MAGA Inc., had in the bank to start last month.But that wasn't enough for Trump. He used taxpayer funding to run television ads celebrating himself, including one nearly identical to a spot from 2024 - the last time he really was on the ballot.It's consistent with a self-centered, second-term approachFrom expanding executive power, to turning the presidency into a profit center for his family, to molding the White House in his own gilded image, Trump's self regard has escalated since he won back the White House."I can do stuff that is unbelievable," he bragged at a rally in Kentucky.Also Read: US midterms: Two Indian-origin face-offs to watch, and why they matterTrump crammed the Oval Office with gold flourishes, demolished the East Wing to build a sprawling ballroom and converted the Rose Garden into a patio space reminiscent of his Mar-a-Lago estate. There's also a new helipad that he showed off to Xi Jinping, China's communist leader, during a recent visit.The president is focused on reshaping Washington as well, dispatching National Guard troops to the streets, closing the Kennedy Center after failed attempts to add his name to the building, planning a towering arch just outside the city and pushing to revamp a century-old public golf course.Trump has wielded his iron grip on the Republican Party in ways that could hurt its chances in some races. He helped Ken Paxton, who has a history of legal and ethical problems, defeat incumbent Sen. John Cornyn in the Texas primary, making the general election campaign against Democrat James Talarico more competitive.Trump also clashed with North Carolina Sen. Tom Tillis, prompting him to retire, and pushed Michael Whatley to run. Now Republicans are bracing to lose the seat to former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper.Trump is 'the dividing line' in the midtermsThe Trump-centric approach backfired during his first term in 2018, when a similar presidential rally barrage didn't stop Democrats from retaking House control.This time, many of the issues that helped Trump win reelection in 2024, such as his handling of the economy, could prove to be liabilities for Republicans.Just 17% of U.S. adults approve of Trump's handling of the cost of living, as the Iran war keeps fuel prices high and stokes inflation fears, according to an AP-NORC poll conducted in late September.The White House points to highlights beyond Trump's personal appeal, like efforts to lower prescription drug prices, stimulate domestic manufacturing, crack down on the U.S.-Mexico border and oppose transgender rights.But longtime Michigan pollster Richard Czuba said the president's decision to focus on himself has prevented Republicans from courting conservative voters disappointed in Trump."He's literally driving people who disagree with him to the Democratic side," Czuba said."The dividing line is how voters feel about Donald Trump," he added. "And there's a whole lot more voters who disapprove of Donald Trump than approve of Donald Trump."A CNN/SSRS poll conducted in mid-October found that about 4 in 10 registered voters suggested they'd think of their vote for Congress as more about sending a message that they oppose Trump. Only about 2 in 10 said they would be sending a message supporting him.Trump's rally whirlwind has kept him on friendly turfEven while hopscotching the country, the president has generally stuck to reliably red states. When he goes to battlegrounds, he mostly visits conservative areas, thus ensuring especially adoring crowds.A pre-speech video likens the president to a global savior, booming repeatedly, "God gave us Trump," and he usually spends more of his speeches repeating past grievances than talking about next week's Election Day.The idea is to energize the Republican base while avoiding backlash in swing states - and also potentially reaching television viewers who see the adulation for Trump and may vote Republican elsewhere around the country."I always cater to my base," Trump recently told the Washington Examiner, when asked if he was focusing too much on sympathetic rallygoers, rather than wooing independents.Trump's endorsement can be enough for some. Cindy Downes, a 67-year-old retiree from North Liberty, Iowa, cast an early ballot for Rep. Ashley Hinson for U.S. Senate and Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks' reelection."The number one reason: POTUS supports them," said Downes, who wore a MAGA hat to a recent campaign event. "I trust him. items.title: James Talarico vows to 'take back Texas'
items.summary: LUBBOCK, Texas: Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico on Tuesday decried a "corruption crisis" he says is plaguing the U.S. political system, competing for the spotlight with President Donald Trump in deeply conservative West Texas ahead of next week's midterm elections.Trump was in Texas for the third time in a month in a last-minute push to back Republican Ken Paxton and block Democrats from notching their first statewide election victory in more than three decades.Talarico took the stage in Lubbock an hour after Trump wrapped up his own speech across town. A seminarian and a former teacher, Talarico reached for metaphors from both the Bible and a famous Texas pastime - Friday night football - to cast himself as an underdog against powerful forces including Trump and Elon Musk, who is bankrolling attack ads against Talarico on Paxton's behalf."We're going to shock the nation and shock the world when we beat the billionaires and take back Texas," Talarico said.Moments earlier, Trump leaned into cultural issues to portray Talarico as too liberal for Texas."He doesn't represent your values, and we can't take a chance," Trump said.Trump won Lubbock County by 40 points in 2024, and won most of the other counties in West Texas by far more. Republicans hope the president's visit will motivate his staunch supporters to vote. The president spoke earlier in Corpus Christi, on the coast of the Gulf of Mexico.As Trump's war in Iran spikes gas prices and adds pressure on Republican candidates across the U.S., he sought to highlight an earlier military operation in Venezuela. Secretary of State Marco Rubio briefly appeared onstage with Trump, who used the trip in part to highlight the arrangement made with Venezuela to process more of its crude oil in Texas refineries.Trump is entering the final week of his last midterms in a frenzied push to shore up Republican strongholds against unusually competitive Democratic candidates. Beyond Texas, he swung through Mississippi, Michigan, Georgia, Florida and Iowa over the past week, and his next stops are Ohio, South Carolina, Florida, Kansas and Iowa again.He won all of these states in 2024.Texas tests Trump's sway over the GOPThe campaign marathon is a bet that while Trump is broadly unpopular, he still holds sway over the GOP's most loyal voters - a bloc whose participation in the elections will be critical.The strategy is facing its fiercest test in Texas, where Talarico has capitalized on the difficult political environment for Republicans and Paxton's history of ethical and legal problems.Trump argued that Paxton was a "good man" and Musk, the world's richest man, has joined Trump's effort to stop Talarico's advance."Talarico is lunatic left," Musk wrote on his social media platform, X, to his 241 million followers, part of a drumbeat of attacks he's posted against the candidate in the race's final days.Musk has headquartered Tesla and SpaceX, as well as himself, in Texas, and is so set on ensuring Republicans hold control of his adopted state that he appears to have sunk at least $158 million into defeating Talarico. Musk gave that much to the Senate Leadership Fund, which then gave the same amount to the Texas PAC, the largest contributor to Paxton's campaign.That's helped make the race one of the most expensive in the country, with over $563 million being spent on advertising between the primary and general elections, according to the ad tracking firm AdImpact.While Musk's investment is a challenge for Talarico, it also falls right into the Democratic campaign's central message. At every stop, Talarico has argued that, for too long, the wealthy and their donations have corrupted politics, and that this corruption has fueled the affordability crisis.Talarico has begun naming Musk in his stump speeches. Paxton tends not to discuss him."He is trying to buy Texas," Talarico said of Musk. "Texas is not for sale."That parallels the Texas governor's race, where Democrat Gina Hinojosa is waging a spirited campaign against GOP Gov. Greg Abbott.Hinojosa has sued to be able to view communications between Musk and Abbott, arguing that their relationship evinces how cozy her opponent is with the ultra-wealthy in Texas.On Monday, a judge ruled that Hinojosa, given her position as a state representative, must be able to review over 1,000 unredacted pages by Thursday.Rubio's visit previews GOP's potential 2028 contestAs the midterms reach the final stretch, the early stages of the next campaign are already surfacing.Rubio, who also serves as Trump's national security adviser, was hitting the road with Trump for the first time as the president barnstorms the country. A State Department official said Rubio was traveling with Trump in his capacity as national security adviser and not secretary of state.The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss the travel plans, said Rubio "needs time with the president on all kinds of issues" and "being on the plane with him gives him a chance to talk to him about these items."Rubio previously ran for president in 2016 and is considered a top prospect in 2028. He has not said whether he will run, and his political activities have been limited since becoming secretary of state.He appeared onstage with Trump briefly in Corpus Christi - and only after Trump repeatedly called on him to come forward."It's an honor to work for the greatest country in the world, for the greatest president in the history of the United States of America," he said before exiting. He was similarly brief in Lubbock, where he kept his remarks to a single sentence.Another top Republican 2028 contender, Vice President JD Vance, has been more active on the campaign trail, stopping in Michigan on Tuesday, where he called the Senate race between Republican Mike Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed a "clash of competing visions."Meanwhile, Pete Buttigieg, the former U.S. transportation secretary and potential 2028 Democratic presidential candidate, was in Mississippi, campaigning on behalf of Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom a day after Trump made his own stop in the deep red state. Both parties have poured money into the state, where Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith faces a surprisingly tough challenge.It's no mystery why gas prices are up, Buttigieg said."It's because Donald Trump decided to start a war and your elected leaders refused to stop him. We can do better than that under new management," he said in Biloxi.In California, Xavier Becerra, a Democrat running for governor, urged voters to reject a voter ID ballot measure, which he said would make it harder for people to vote."We want democracy not just to shine, but be so resilient and so strong that Donald Trump cannot knock California down," Becerra said in San Francisco.

Globally, total number of heatwave days decreased from 2024's historical high of 15.3 billion person-days for older adults and 2.3 billion person-days for infants. Markets regulator Sebi on Tuesday extended the deadline by six months, till April 27, 2027, for debenture trustees to comply with requirements governing activities that fall outside its regulatory purview.
Under Regulation 9C of the Sebi (Debenture Trustees) Regulations, 1993, a debenture trustee holding a valid certificate of registration is required to transfer activities not regulated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) to separate business units within a prescribed timeline.

Sebi had initially given six months for compliance. Subsequently, in April 2026, the regulator granted an additional six months, extending the deadline to October 27, 2026, following industry representations highlighting operational challenges in establishing the necessary systems and processes.

items.title: US lawmakers warn banks, ports of probe over Russian diesel imports
items.summary:
A bipartisan group of US lawmakers has warned American banks, port authorities and fuel distributors that importing Russian diesel could invite legal action and congressional investigations.
In letters to the heads of major financial institutions, ports and fuel distributors, the lawmakers said companies facilitating imports in violation of US law could face criminal and civil liability.
The letters came amid reports that shipments of Russian diesel were headed to American shores after President Donald Trump earlier this month granted a waiver allowing Moscow to supply diesel to global markets, including the US.
The lawmakers cited Section 2 of the Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022, which generally prohibits the importation of Russian-origin energy products, including diesel fuel.
Such imports are allowed only after the President certifies to Congress that Russia has ceased all military hostilities in Ukraine and that it poses no immediate threat to NATO members.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued the notice after hearing senior advocate Madhavi Divan, appearing for the Digital News Publishers Association.

items.title: SC collegium recommends four judges for appointment as HC chief justices
items.summary:
The Supreme Court Collegium headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has recommended to the Centre the appointment of four judges as chief justices of various high courts.
The collegium, also comprising Justices Vikram Nath and B V Nagarathna, held its meeting on October 26 and recommended the name of Justice P Sam Koshy of the Telangana High Court for appointment as Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court.
Justice Manash Ranjan Pathak, currently serving at the Gujarat High Court, has been recommended for appointment as Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court.
The Collegium has also recommended Justice Tapabrata Chakraborty of the Calcutta High Court for appointment as Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court.
Justice Sudhir Singh of the Patna High Court has been recommended for appointment as Chief Justice of the Uttarakhand High Court.

items.title: 25% of S Asian Americans who backed Trump plan to back Democrats: Survey
items.summary:
At least 25 per cent of South Asian Americans who voted for US President Donald Trump in the 2024 presidential election plan to support Democratic candidates in the November 3 midterm elections, according to a survey.
The survey, conducted by advocacy group Indian American Impact, lists cost of living (65 per cent), healthcare (53 per cent), jobs and wages (33 per cent) and education (28 per cent) as key issues for the midterm polls.
Among 800 South Asian registered voters surveyed, 87 per cent were Indian-Americans and the remaining 13 per cent were Pakistani, Bangladeshi, Sri Lankan, Nepali, Bhutanese, Maldivian, Afghani, Khmer, and Burmese people.
Among those who voted for Kamala Harris in the 2024 presidential election, 96 per cent plan to cast their ballots in favour of a Democratic candidate in the upcoming polls.
The survey found that 67 per cent of South Asian Americans who voted for Trump still backed the Republicans, but 25 per cent said they would support Democrats.

items.title: Wheat sowing lags at 11,000 ha amid deficient monsoon, irrigation concerns
items.summary:
Wheat sowing has just commenced in a few states, with coverage at 11,000 hectare so far, against 27,000 hectare in the year-ago period, amid a deficient southwest monsoon, according to Agriculture Ministry data.
"Wheat sowing has just commenced in a few states," the ministry said while releasing the sowing data as of October 23.
Wheat, a major rabi crop, is generally sown in October-November and harvested in March-April. The crop was sown in 336 lakh hectare in the 2025-26 crop year (July-June).
The ministry has set a wheat production target of 121 million tonnes for the 2026-27 crop year, following a record output of 120.7 million tonnes in the previous year.
The southwest monsoon (June-September) was 13 per cent deficient as per the Met Department. A weak monsoon leaves less residual soil moisture and lower water levels in reservoirs and canals at the start of the rabi season.
